Roll a Dungeons & Dragons character: six abilities, each the best three of four dice, and hitpoints from the constitution's modifier.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/dnd-character) (MIT). Listed under [Games & Simulation](/examples/?subject=games-and-simulation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: dnd_character.nomi
//# A Dungeons & Dragons character with six random abilities, each the best
//# three of four six-sided dice, and hitpoints from its constitution.

import std/random.Generator

/// A character's six abilities and its hitpoints.
pub struct Character {
    strength: Int
    dexterity: Int
    constitution: Int
    intelligence: Int
    wisdom: Int
    charisma: Int
    hitpoints: Int
}

/// The modifier an ability `score` gives: half its distance from 10,
/// rounded down.
pub fn modifier(score: Int) -> Int {
    Int.floor_div(score - 10, 2)
}

/// One ability score: four dice rolled, the lowest dropped, the rest added.
pub fn ability() -> Generator<Int> {
    Generator.int(1, 6)
    |> Generator.list(4)
    |> Generator.map(fn rolls -> rolls |> Iter.sort() |> Iter.drop(1) |> Iter.sum())
}

/// A character with six abilities drawn in order, strength first.
pub fn character() -> Generator<Character> {
    ability()
    |> Generator.list(6)
    |> Generator.map(fn scores -> {
        case scores {
            [strength, dexterity, constitution, intelligence, wisdom, charisma] -> #{
                strength,
                dexterity,
                constitution,
                intelligence,
                wisdom,
                charisma,
                hitpoints: 10 + modifier(constitution),
            }
            _ -> unreachable "Generator.list(6) draws six scores"
        }
    })
}

// FILE: dnd_character_test.nomi
import {
    std/random.{Generator, Seed}
    dnd_character
    dnd_character.Character
}

/// The values `generator` draws from the seeds 1 to 200.
fn draws<T>(generator: Generator<T>) -> List<T> {
    1..=200
    |> Iter.map(fn n -> {
        #(value, _seed) = Generator.step(generator, Seed.from_int(n))
        value
    })
    |> Iter.to_list()
}

fn in_range?(score: Int) -> Bool {
    score >= 3 and score <= 18
}

fn valid?(character: Character) -> Bool {
    abilities = [
        character.strength,
        character.dexterity,
        character.constitution,
        character.intelligence,
        character.wisdom,
        character.charisma,
    ]

    Iter.all?(abilities, in_range?)
        and character.hitpoints == 10 + dnd_character.modifier(character.constitution)
}

test "ability modifier" {
    cases = [
        #("ability modifier for score 3 is -4", 3, -4),
        #("ability modifier for score 4 is -3", 4, -3),
        #("ability modifier for score 5 is -3", 5, -3),
        #("ability modifier for score 6 is -2", 6, -2),
        #("ability modifier for score 7 is -2", 7, -2),
        #("ability modifier for score 8 is -1", 8, -1),
        #("ability modifier for score 9 is -1", 9, -1),
        #("ability modifier for score 10 is 0", 10, 0),
        #("ability modifier for score 11 is 0", 11, 0),
        #("ability modifier for score 12 is +1", 12, 1),
        #("ability modifier for score 13 is +1", 13, 1),
        #("ability modifier for score 14 is +2", 14, 2),
        #("ability modifier for score 15 is +2", 15, 2),
        #("ability modifier for score 16 is +3", 16, 3),
        #("ability modifier for score 17 is +3", 17, 3),
        #("ability modifier for score 18 is +4", 18, 4),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, score, expected), description {
        assert dnd_character.modifier(score) == expected
    }
}

test "random ability is within range" {
    assert dnd_character.ability()
        |> draws()
        |> Iter.all?(in_range?)
}

test "random character is valid" {
    assert dnd_character.character()
        |> draws()
        |> Iter.all?(valid?)
}

test "each ability is only calculated once" {
    seed = Seed.from_int(7)
    #(first, _) = Generator.step(dnd_character.character(), seed)
    #(again, _) = Generator.step(dnd_character.character(), seed)

    assert first == again
}
```

## How it's written

- Randomness is `std/random`'s: `ability` and `character` answer a `Generator`, a recipe that `Generator.step` runs against a `Seed`. Nothing here reads entropy, so the tests draw from fixed seeds and every run checks the same 200 characters.
- An ability is `Generator.int(1, 6)` drawn four times with `Generator.list`, then sorted, the lowest dropped with `Iter.drop(1)`, and the rest summed.
- A character is six abilities drawn with `Generator.list(6)` and taken apart with one list pattern, in the order the struct declares them. The other arm is `unreachable`, since `Generator.list(6)` always draws six.
- `Character` is a struct, so an ability is a field read and is calculated once by construction. The two canonical "each ability is only calculated once" cases (strength alone, and every ability) are one test: the same seed draws an equal character twice.
- `modifier` is `Int.floor_div(score - 10, 2)`: the modifier rounds down, and `/` truncates toward zero, so a score of 3 would give `-3` where the modifier is `-4`.
- The canonical modifier cases are one `subtests` table; the property cases ("within range", "is valid") check every draw from seeds 1 to 200.
